title: Restructure trilingual installation information architecture
outOfScope: Installer runtime behavior, release publishing, signing implementation, branch-protection automation, and calibration-session schema behavior
Changing current Capability Truth statuses without new implementation evidence
Deleting historical Work Item archives or user-owned worktree changes

sources.reason: Current English installation entry demonstrates the overloaded all-reader information architecture.
Current Chinese primary installation route subject to the user feedback.
Current Japanese route must remain semantically aligned for the primary adopter audience.
Historic WI-10 implementation evidence; it does not prove the newly requested information architecture is delivered.
Authoritative documentation-role architecture to update for the new reader-separated routes.
Authoritative current requirements: simple Work Item-centered adoption, reader-separated detail, and beginner usability.

rawUserRequest: The trilingual installation document is too difficult because it exposes governance, security-audit, calibration-session, and maintainer material before a first-time adopter can act. Rebuild it as a simple Happy Path: Runtime installation followed by a calibration/configuration Work Item. Already-installed repositories also start Work Items directly. Separate strict release/supply-chain verification, calibration guidance, calibration internals, troubleshooting, and document-maintenance content. Preserve the safety model, keep English/Chinese/Japanese semantically aligned, and make the result usable by someone with no programming experience without requiring knowledge of Session, Candidate, digest, or phase record.

declaredIntent.summary: Replace the overloaded trilingual installation guide with a Work Item-centered, beginner-safe documentation architecture while retaining fail-closed governance evidence in reader-specific routes.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A first-time adopter opens any of the three installation home pages.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The reader sees only prerequisites, six-stage map, short action/purpose/result/STOP guidance, installation completion, and a calibration Work Item handoff; advanced internal terms are absent from the happy path.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add structural tests for all three home pages, line budget, required stage headings, short prompt blocks, and prohibited advanced-internal vocabulary outside linked advanced routes.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A Runtime has just been installed or the repository is already installed.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The first path creates a calibration/configuration Work Item after install; the existing-install path starts the requested Work Item directly without replaying bootstrap prompts.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add trilingual route assertions that distinguish first installation from installed-repository Work Item handoff and retain the current ai-start command evidence.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An enterprise/security reader needs release verification, a maintainer needs document checks, or an adopter encounters a failure.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Each reader reaches the named security, maintenance, or troubleshooting document through a valid link; the home page does not duplicate its protocol.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add negative link, missing-document, duplicate-protocol, and retained-boundary mutations to the documentation metadata suite.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A translation adds convenience wording that weakens a safety boundary.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The multilingual checker rejects missing Unknown, no-silent-fallback, no-overwrite, separated-permission, manual-activation, or independent-owner/reviewer statements.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend mutation tests across English, Chinese, and Japanese routes and regenerate source-bound capability assessments after all text changes.

riskAssessment.reason: Moving governance detail out of the beginner path can accidentally weaken visible safety boundaries or cause the three languages to diverge; mechanical route, link, and retained-boundary checks are required.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly approved continuous execution and specified the desired information architecture and Work Item-centered adoption boundary.

preReviewWarnings: Keep the happy path short without making the safety model less strict; relocate rather than delete advanced evidence and recovery guidance.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A1: English, Chinese, and Japanese installation home pages are beginner-first happy paths of approximately 150–250 lines, each explaining the six visible stages, prerequisites, one purpose/result/STOP-oriented action per stage, installation completion, and the explicit next Work Item.

A2: All three first-install paths finish Runtime installation by creating a calibration/configuration Work Item; all already-installed paths start the relevant Work Item directly without repeating first-install prompts.

A3: Strict supply-chain/release verification, calibration guidance, calibration-session internals, troubleshooting, and maintainer proofreading are separated into their named reader-specific documents and linked from—not duplicated in—the installation home pages.

A4: The beginner pages preserve visible fail-closed boundaries: Unknown is not guessed, no silent Release fallback or overwrite, permissions remain separated, and no automatic calibration activation or self-proved Owner/Reviewer approval is claimed.
A5: README and Documentation Architecture expose the new route map; English, Chinese, and Japanese routes have aligned meaning and valid internal links.

A6: Machine checks reject oversized/advanced-internal beginner pages, missing Work Item handoff, missing split documents, broken links, missing trilingual routes, and loss of the retained safety boundaries.
A7: Focused documentation regressions, full quality, active Outcome, archive, PR, Hosted CI, merge, closure, and branch cleanup complete before Dependabot #444 resumes.
guidelines: Use progressive disclosure: first-time adopters see only the next safe action, expected result, and STOP condition; advanced material remains available by explicit links.
Use Work Item as the common post-install and installed-repository control boundary; do not make prompts a substitute for governed lifecycle execution.
Maintain English, Chinese, and Japanese semantic parity; Japanese is a full supported route, not a summary.
Preserve current safety claims and limitations exactly in the appropriate advanced document; do not imply that documentation alone creates runtime guarantees.

intent.problem: The current trilingual installation pages are technically comprehensive but overload first-time adopters with Runtime, Calibration, Hosted CI, Session, Candidate, phase-record, evidence, and maintainer material before they can install. This makes the adoption path difficult to understand and obscures that calibration and later governance belong in Work Items.
constraints: Keep the governing safety model fail-closed and do not delete advanced evidence or recovery information.
Do not require a reader with no programming background to understand Session, Candidate, digest, or phase-record internals to install.
After first Runtime installation, calibration must be initiated in a Work Item; already-installed repositories start Work Items directly.
Keep all three language routes complete and semantically aligned.
intent.rationale: AI Cockpit's North Star requires heavy governance with light human operation. Separating reader paths lets Runtime and Work Item controls carry the protocol while the homepage guides a beginner safely to the next action.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: Set only when a human explicitly approves restricted governance paths.
